Oral Communication

Make two large groups of the class students; one of them to act as the Ralph's group and the other as Jack's band. Give them an issue or some issues to be resolved by them. Each group should forward its suggestions and proposals regarding the issue(s).

Vocabulary and Grammar

A. Look for in a Thesaurus and tell whether each pair of words are synonyms or antonyms.

1. agree, disagree ____

2. cold, freezing ____

3. easy, difficult ____

4. argue, squabble ____

5. guess, estimate ____

6. bottom, top ____

7. tired, energetic ____

8. huge, gigantic ____

9. sink, float ____

10. windy, calm ____

11. noisy, quiet ____

12. unhappy, sad ____

B. Identify the following sentences as Simple, Compound and Complex.

1. We were playing in the garden when the guests arrived.

2. She put on her coat and went out.

3. I can’t figure out what he wants.

4. You don’t look happy to see me.

5. The cat saw the puppies playing in the garden.

6. She leaned out of the window.

7. You shouldn’t have done this to me.

8. They tried very hard but they couldn’t win the match.

9. Who let the cat in?

10. Although it was raining, we went for a walk.

C. Write the strongest word of the pair given in the parenthesis in the given blank of each sentence.

1. The flowers were ____ in the garden. (beautiful, pretty)

2. We had a ____ dinner at the restaurant. (good, delicious)

3. The glass plated ____ to the ground. (fell, crashed)

4. She ____ hello to the teacher. (said, whispered)

5. The ____ cat sat on the fence. (starving, hungry)

6. He slept on the ____ bed. (hard, firm)

7. The children will ____ out the door when the bell rings. (dash, march)

8. Salim was ____ with his brother. (cross, furious)

D. Write the indirect narration in the 'Indirect Speech column' for the sentences given in 'Direct Speech column'.
